placements.why: The content describes pipeline behavior for identifier generation and file commitment — an architectural concern about how the system is structured to handle operational requirements when explicit inputs are missing.
placements.title: System structure and pipeline behavior
placements.theme: The pipeline's design must handle operational requirements — identification, fallback mechanisms, and file commitment — through structured, reliable mechanisms.

placements.title: Identification Derived From Content When No Explicit Id Is Supplied
placements.theme: When no explicit identifier is provided, the pipeline must generate a slug from memory content through LLM id-generation or deterministic slugify fallback to ensure successful file commitment.
placements.why: src-1 asserts the absence of an explicit id field, and src-2 directs the pipeline to produce a slug from content via two fallback mechanisms and commit the file. Together they support the theme that identification must be content-derived when no explicit id is given — a subject future envelopes will keep feeding as the pipeline's identification behavior evolves.
